overview: A one-page Department of State list of papers inventories material filed on Japanese news-gathering agencies and press activity in China in 1931–1932. Its entries point to reports from Shanghai and Tientsin, a State Department memorandum, and cross-references concerning Japanese newspaper opposition, the organization and purposes of a Press Union, the alleged capture of Japanese newspapermen, John N. Heijbroek’s reported mission to secure their release, and examples of misinformation disseminated by Japanese news agencies and reported from Peiping.

subfiles.title: List of papers on Japanese news-gathering agencies in China
subfiles.about: An index identifies reports, memoranda, and cross-references concerning Japanese newspapers, press organizations, captured correspondents, and misinformation in China.
subfiles.summary: The sheet inventories several papers dating principally from 1931–1932. It records opposition involving Japanese newspapers in China and notes that the Japanese Legation had been instructed to negotiate a settlement. Other entries concern a Press Union circular, Japanese newspapermen reportedly captured by Chinese forces, John N. Heijbroek’s alleged effort on behalf of Japanese authorities to secure four men’s release, and misinformation circulated by Japanese news agencies and documented by the Legation at Peiping. It also supplies cross-references to files 894.00 P R/41, 798.94/3268, and 894.20293/15.

interest: This sheet is useful as a map to a dispersed body of State Department reporting on Japanese press operations in early-1930s China. Although the underlying papers are not present here, the index links diplomatic negotiations, press organization, disputed detentions, alleged covert activity, and official concern about misinformation. Its archival cross-references may help historians reconstruct related material filed elsewhere in the decimal system.
